transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-12-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: 11 minutes
Attendees: Nina Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Samir Khan (Lodestar Head of Security), Elena Ruiz (Lodestar CTO), Daniel Park (Lodestar DevOps)

Summary: High-level security intake focused on hosted vs dedicated vs private deploy options, KMS/bring-your-own-key, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs and retention. Customer concerned about data residency and SOC2/ISO evidence; wants network/topology details for dedicated and an on-prem proof-of-concept path.

Topics: SOC2/ISO, SSO/SCIM, RBAC model, audit log retention and export, encryption and KMS BYOK, dedicated capacity networking, private VPC/on-prem package, performance tradeoffs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Nina Patel: Okay hi everyone thanks for joining, we're recording this to capture the notes. I'm Nina, AE on the account, Marcus will do the deeper infra stuff.
[00:08] Samir Khan: Hi Nina thanks. Quick note we, we have limited time so we'll try to be concise — got a security checklist to run down.
[00:15] Marcus Lee: Great — Marcus Lee here, solutions engineer. Today I'll focus on the hosting and encryption bits.
[00:22] Elena Ruiz: Quick context from our side — we're evaluating Redwood to power our analyst assistant. There's PII mixed in the prompts and EU customers so data residency is a hard constraint.
[00:34] Daniel Park: We run primarily in AWS with some GCP. We use HashiCorp Vault for secrets and AWS KMS with HSM-backed keys for crypto.
[00:44] Nina Patel: Thanks. Can you tell us which deployment path you prefer — Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, or Private (VPC/on-prem)?
[00:53] Samir Khan: Private is ideal but might be heavy. Realistically Dedicated in our VPC if we can BYOK and get immutable audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[01:03] Marcus Lee: That tracks. For Dedicated we do VPC peering or private endpoints; for Private we have an on-prem bundle for air-gapped installs. Dedicated gives isolation with less ops than full on-prem.
[01:14] Samir Khan: On BYOK — can we keep keys in our HSM and still run inference?
[01:20] Marcus Lee: Yes, we support BYOK. For AWS KMS/Azure KV/GCP KMS we do envelope encryption; the root key stays in your KMS. For on-prem HSM integration we can talk KMIP and agent-based approaches — sometimes docs transcribe KMIP as 'K-MIP' by mistake.
[01:35] Elena Ruiz: For audit evidence — we need key usage logs and admin activity with tamper-proof retention.
[01:41] Marcus Lee: We emit audit events for decryption ops and admin actions. You can forward logs to S3 or your SIEM. We support S3 Object Lock for write-once storage and can stream to Splunk/Datadog.
[01:53] Daniel Park: Do logs include prompt text by default? That would be a huge no for us.
[01:58] Marcus Lee: By default Hosted redacts PII; for Dedicated you control logging. We can log metadata only — request IDs, token counts, timestamps, but not prompt contents unless you ask. We'll include redaction rules in the follow-up.
[02:11] Samir Khan: Retention windows — our legal wants 7 years for admin logs. Can you set per-log retention?
[02:17] Marcus Lee: Yes, retention is configurable per stream. Hosted has defaults; Dedicated and Private allow custom retention via S3 lifecycle or SIEM retention.
[02:27] Elena Ruiz: SOC2 and ISO — can you share artifacts? Do they cover Dedicated/Private?
[02:33] Nina Patel: We'll send the SOC2 Type II attestation and ISO27001 cert after the call. SOC2 primarily covers hosted services; Dedicated has contractual controls and Private requires customer responsibilities, but we provide runbooks and evidence for the parts we operate.
[02:47] Samir Khan: For SSO and provisioning we use Okta — need SAML 2.0, SP-initiated, and SCIM for group sync. How's the integration?
[02:56] Marcus Lee: Full SAML 2.0 support, SP and IdP initiated flows, SCIM for provisioning and group sync. RBAC maps from Okta groups to Redwood roles and you can scope roles per environment.
[03:08] Daniel Park: We need separation between prod and staging teams and auditors should have read-only views without secret access.
[03:14] Marcus Lee: Fine-grained RBAC is supported — admin, infra, dev, auditor roles; auditors get read-only dashboards and can't access secrets or plaintext.
[03:25] Samir Khan: About network topology — for Dedicated can we use VPC endpoints so there is no public egress for serving nodes?
[03:32] Marcus Lee: Absolutely; we support VPC peering and private endpoints. Access to S3 can be via VPC endpoints and we recommend restricting egress through proxy if external calls are needed.
[03:42] Elena Ruiz: On the hosted side, do you ever call external APIs automatically?
[03:47] Marcus Lee: No external calls are made without explicit configuration for tool-calling. By default runtime execution is contained.
[03:55] Daniel Park: For private installs, what inbound ports are required? Our firewall is strict.
[04:00] Marcus Lee: Private on-prem installs require limited management ports for deployment; you can opt for an air-gapped install which avoids outbound connections. We'll share the port list.
[04:10] Samir Khan: Pen testing — are we allowed to run pentests?
[04:14] Nina Patel: Yes, we permit customer-led pentests under coordination. We'll provide a pentest policy and required notice windows.
[04:22] Samir Khan: Model weights and IP controls — will Redwood cache third-party weights that could raise IP concerns?
[04:27] Marcus Lee: We host a curated model catalog, but customers can bring their own weights. For Dedicated we can store weights in your S3 or in your VPC; contractual terms cover IP restrictions.
[04:38] Elena Ruiz: How long to onboard Dedicated vs Private?
[04:42] Marcus Lee: Dedicated typically 2–4 weeks including peering and RBAC setup; Private on-prem often 6–12 weeks depending on ops and air-gap requirements.
[04:52] Samir Khan: One final compliance ask — immutability (WORM) for audit logs. Can you support that?
[04:58] Marcus Lee: Yes, S3 Object Lock or forwarding to your SIEM with immutable retention is supported.
[05:05] Nina Patel: Quick recap of artifacts we'll send: SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 cert, security whitepaper, on-prem runbook, Dedicated network diagram, retention matrix, SSO/SCIM guide, pentest policy, and Dedicated pricing.
[05:18] Samir Khan: Please include the exact log schema and the redaction settings so legal can review.
[05:24] Marcus Lee: We'll attach sample log schema and a redaction guide.
[05:29] Elena Ruiz: Also want a benchmark with our sample load and keys integrated; that would clarify perf and logging behavior.
[05:36] Nina Patel: We'll schedule a 2-hour benchmark slot next week. Marcus will run it in a sandbox VPC.
[05:43] Daniel Park: For KMS integration, confirm that plaintext root key never leaves our KMS?
[05:48] Marcus Lee: Correct — envelope encryption ensures the root key never leaves. We document rotation and ephemeral DEK issuance.
[05:56] Samir Khan: Sounds good — I'll send the regulatory list and specific retention asks.
[06:01] Nina Patel: Thanks Samir. We'll follow up EOD tomorrow with the compliance packet and diagrams.
[06:07] Samir Khan: Appreciate it.
[06:10] Elena Ruiz: Thanks everyone.
[06:12] Daniel Park: Bye.

End of transcript.
